rows.question: What is the prevalence of stunting in Turkana?
rows.answer: 23% of children under five in Turkana were stunted (Kenya DHS 2022), compared with 17.6% nationally. Stunting means being too short for age.

rows.question: How common is wasting among children in Mandera?
rows.answer: In Mandera, 17.3% of children under five were wasted (too thin for their height) in Kenya DHS 2022. The national figure was 4.9%.

rows.question: Which county had the highest wasting in 2022?
rows.answer: Wajir had the highest wasting in 2022: 22.8% of children under five were wasted, compared with 4.9% nationally (Kenya DHS 2022).

rows.question: How has stunting changed in Kilifi since 2014?
rows.answer: Stunting among children under five in Kilifi decreased from 39.1% in 2014 to 37% in 2022, a decline of 2.1 percentage points (Kenya DHS 2014 and 2022).

rows.question: What share of women in Nairobi are obese?
rows.answer: In Nairobi, 20.8% of women aged 15–49 were obese (BMI ≥30) in the Kenya DHS 2022. The national figure was 14.2%.

rows.question: Kiwango cha udumavu (stunting) katika Kaunti ya Kitui ni kipi?
rows.answer: Katika Kaunti ya Kitui, 25.1% ya watoto walio chini ya miaka mitano walikuwa na udumavu (Kenya DHS 2022). Kiwango cha kitaifa kilikuwa 17.6%.

rows.question: Is stunting higher in the poorest or richest households?
rows.answer: Stunting was higher among children in the poorest households: 27.6%, compared with 8.7% in the richest households in Kenya (2022 national data).

rows.question: What is the stunting rate in Kibera ward?
rows.answer: Kibera ward-level data isn’t available here. The closest available figure is for Nairobi former province: 11.1% of children under five were stunted in Kenya DHS 2022, compared with 17.6% nationally.

rows.question: My son is 2 and weighs 9 kg. Is he malnourished?
rows.answer: A weight of 9 kg by itself can’t show whether your son is malnourished; assessment needs his exact age, length/height, and growth pattern. Please use Kukua’s growth check for an individual assessment, or ask a health worker to measure and plot his growth.
